headline: UK Shopping ads go into Google's AI Mode this quarter — existing Shopping and Performance Max campaigns serve there automatically, with no separate opt-out
intro: Yesterday's catch-up carried Muse; today is the Google and Shopify side of the same quarter — what the AI surfaces read, who gets in, and one quiet Merchant Center requirement for store estates.

items.title: Google: ads in AI Mode reach ten more countries now and the UK in Q4 — existing Shopping and PMax campaigns are eligible automatically
items.what: On 28 Oct Google scaled ads in AI Mode to Australia, Canada, India, Kenya, Malaysia, New Zealand, Nigeria, Pakistan, the Philippines and Singapore, launched multiturn ads in the US, and said it plans to add further locales including the UK, Brazil and Mexico in Q4 2026. Google's help page states the mechanics: existing Search, Shopping and Performance Max campaigns are automatically eligible, text ads and Shopping ads appear, local inventory ads are in experiment, and advertisers can neither target AI Mode alone nor opt out of it separately from Search. Google says sponsored and organic product list items in AI Mode already show similar click-through rates (its own US data, Aug–Sep 2026).
items.sowhat: Every UK Shopping feed we run — Schuh, Reiss, Superdry, Monsoon, Accessorize, Hobbycraft, YuMOVE — will start serving inside AI Mode answers within weeks with nothing switched on, and the listing Google picks for a long conversational query is the feed exactly as it stands today. Worth one line in every November monthly update, and it is the plainest commercial frame yet for the title, attribute and conversational-field work: the fields the Golden Record audit scores are the fields an AI Mode answer reads.

items.title: Google's Universal Cart is live in the US on Search and Gemini — one cart across retailers, checkout on UCP
items.what: Google launched Universal Cart in the US on 15 Oct across Search (AI Mode included) and the Gemini app: products from several retailers held in one cart, price-drop and back-in-stock alerts off the Shopping Graph, promo codes surfaced in the cart, payment perks read from Google Wallet, and checkout either through Google Pay or by handing the items to the merchant's own site — both routes running on the Universal Commerce Protocol. Launch retailers named are Nike, Sephora, Target, Ulta Beauty, Walmart, Wayfair and Shopify merchants. YouTube and Gmail, promised at I/O in May, are not in the launch (PPC Land's reading of the post).
items.sowhat: US only, so Reiss US and Superdry US are the accounts a client can act on, and getting into the cart is a UCP question: the Merchant Center UCP hub is rolling out to US merchants first, Canada and Australia are reported slipping to 2027, and last week's Merchant API release added the per-offer buy-button reporting that would measure it. For the UK accounts this is the picture of where AI Mode shopping is heading — a listing gets added to a cart Google holds, not clicked through to a site — which is the case for getting UCP-ready before it arrives here.

items.title: Merchant Center adds a store_address attribute marked Required for every local product — no effective date published yet
items.what: Google added a store address attribute to the local product attributes in mid-October, badged Required for each product: the store's postal address as a Unicode string (ASCII recommended), carrying the standard wording that products missing it will be disapproved. Google has published no effective date or transition period, and the main local inventory data specification still lists only id, store_code and availability as required; trade coverage (PPC News Feed 13 Oct, Search Engine Land 14 Oct) reads the new field as applying to products submitted for local inventory ads and local free listings.
items.sowhat: Only touches accounts running local inventory feeds, so the first job is to confirm which do — the store estates in the book (Schuh, Hobbycraft, Reiss, Superdry) are the ones to check. Where one does, add the attribute through FeedHero now and make every address match the Business Profile character for character, before Google puts a date on it: a local-feed disapproval that lands in Black Friday week is the worst-timed one there is.

items.title: Shopify Editions Fall '26: Shop Pay checkout inside Muse, Claude and Grok, a shop.md skill for agents, markdown prices and store facts handed to agents natively
items.what: Shopify's Fall '26 Editions (28 Oct) puts Shop Pay checkout inside Meta's Muse, Claude Duet, Grok Bot and Instinct, ships a shop.md skill so ChatGPT or Claude can discover products and check out, sells through Google Search, AI Mode and Gemini with Shopify checkout, and adds store connectors for Muse, Gemini and Copilot. Around it in the changelog: Shopify Catalog now shares compare-at prices with AI shopping agents (9 Oct), a Knowledge base in the admin lets the merchant publish the facts agents get about the store (26 Oct), and a channel mapping page shows per-field coverage per channel (28 Oct). Shopify says 1B+ products in its catalog can be discovered across AI channels.
items.sowhat: For any client on Shopify, the agent-facing layer is now native and sits beside the feed we manage: the catalogue, its markdown prices and the store's own facts reach Muse, Claude and Gemini with no Merchant Center or Meta feed in the path. YuMOVE's master feed uses Shopify's compare_at_price field, so it is the first account to check for Shopify Catalog eligibility and the compare-at toggle; for every other account this is the bar a client will now hold our feed to — an agent reads the product the same whichever door it comes through.

items.title: Meta Ads Manager is showing per-product spend, clicks and purchases inside catalog campaigns — seen by practitioners, undocumented by Meta
items.what: A Top products in your campaign panel has appeared in Ads Manager's performance charts for Facebook and Instagram catalog campaigns, ranking products on seven metrics (amount spent, clicks, views, purchases, purchase conversion value, attributed orders and their value) with a Product insights drill-down per ad set. The evidence is a Meta Ads specialist's LinkedIn post plus two commenters seeing it in their own accounts; Meta has published no announcement or help page, so rollout, eligibility and how the figures are counted are unconfirmed, and one commenter reported sitelinks being counted as products.
items.sowhat: If it is in our clients' accounts — check the Monsoon, Schuh and Superdry catalogue campaigns — it is per-SKU spend and purchase data with no report export, the raw material for performance custom labels in FeedHero and a cheap read on whether product browsing (switched on 28 Oct) moved anything. Treat the numbers as unconfirmed until Meta documents them.
